items.title: 52986_Lawrence Brown oral history interview
items.q: At the time you joined Duke, the 12 members of the band were Johnny Hodges, Barney Bigard... Right. Uh-huh.

ctx.x: How about other members of the band? Who were some of the other composers in the band?

Well, let me see -- Harry Carney, of course Johnny. And Barney, Tricky -- that was Tricky Sam, Cootie and most everybody did something. Freddy Jenkins -- he wrote several tunes before he had to leave. And I've never heard anything about what happened to them so I don't know, but everybody, with the exception of the guitar player, used to contribute in the musical side of the aggregation.

items.title: 68113_Barney Bigard oral history interview
items.q: Lawrence Brown was in it... Lawrence Brown and Otto Hardwick... Duke made a tune out of it.

ctx.x: Yeah, and I had to play the bridge in that (humming). Sure. Just like Lawrence Brown and Otto Hardwick, they made Sophisticated Lady.

items.title: 68113_Barney Bigard oral history interview
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] And I think, I heard that Lawrence Brown was called "Sweetie"? >> [INTERVIEWEE] Sweetie.

items.title: 68113_Barney Bigard oral history interview
items.q: He helps everybody. The man, he -- money doesn't mean nothing to him.

ctx.x: He helps everybody. The man, he -- money doesn't mean nothing to him.

He wanted a kid so bad, and -- this is real funny. He had a little gal called Sweet -- Sweetie-something and she got pregnant but not by Louie. But Louie thought it was by him because she was telling him that, you know? And, oh, he was proud. He's going to be the daddy.

So he had a bag. We were traveling by bus now, and he had a bag and all the -- when he was getting ready to go to sleep -- all the change he had in his pocket plus dollars he'd take it, put it in his bag. I asked him what he was doing that for. He said, 'That's for my kid when it's born.' Okay, so by the time this kid was born that bag was stuffed with coins and dollars and fives and tens, just stuffed.
